name: Gaius
overview: The name Gaius appears in several New Testament contexts, highlighting faithful believers who supported the early church and the apostles. One Gaius, a Macedonian and companion of Paul, was seized during a riot in Ephesus, demonstrating his close association with Paul's missionary efforts (Acts 19:29). Another Gaius from Derbe accompanied Paul on his travels through Macedonia into Asia (Acts 20:4). In Rome, a Gaius hosted the whole church, reflecting his role as a generous and hospitable believer (Romans 16:23). Additionally, the third epistle of John is addressed to a beloved Gaius, commended for his walk in the truth and spiritual prosperity (3 John 1:1-3). These references collectively portray Gaius as a devoted follower of Christ, exemplifying faithfulness, hospitality, and steadfastness in the gospel.
